 Closings and Delays 3 weather alerts in effect Snow in the forecast for Western North Carolina as big temp drop approaches 
 Expect a big change starting Thursday, lasting through weekend 
 WBTV's First Alert Weather team is tracking a major drop in temperatures that's expected to bring the season's first snow to the North Carolina mountains. By Lisa Villegas Published : Nov. 11, 2026 at 11:24 PM EST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CHARLOTTE, N.C. (WBTV) - The Charlotte region is gearing up for its first taste of winter this season: Snow is in the forecast for mountain communities starting this week.
 After enjoying some beautiful November warmth, the Carolinas are about to feel a big change starting Thursday. A strong cold front is opening the door for the coldest air of the season, bringing gusty winds, a chance for mountain snow and several mornings near or below freezing. 
 Here’s a look at the forecast, as of Wednesday, Nov. 11.
 First snowflakes of season possible in mountains 
 A strong cold front will move through on Thursday, Nov. 12, sending temperatures tumbling from the 70s into the 50s by Friday. 
 Gusty winds will make the change feel even more noticeable, especially in the mountains. 
 The first snowflakes of the season could fly in our highest mountain elevations. Snow showers will be possible Thursday into early Saturday, mainly along the North Carolina and Tennessee border. 
 Some of the highest peaks could pick up 1-3 inches of snow, although most mountain communities will see much less.
 3 freezing mornings ahead 
 WBTV’s First Alert Weather team has issued first alerts for three upcoming mornings, due to a significant drop in temperatures.
 Here’s what to expect:
 Saturday morning: Around 35 degrees in Charlotte, with freezing temperatures possible in surrounding communities. 
 Sunday morning: Our coldest morning. Charlotte could dip to 31 degrees, bringing our first freeze of the season. 
 Monday morning: Another chilly start near 34 degrees as everyone heads back to work and the kids head to the bus stop. 
 It’s time to pull out the heavier coats, bring sensitive plants indoors, and make sure everyone is ready for those frosty mornings.
 Cold, but with sunshine 
 We’re expecting plenty of sunshine this weekend, despite the cold temperatures. 
 Afternoon highs will stay in the 50s, which is below normal for this time of year. 
 So while the weather will be dry and bright, you’ll definitely want those extra layers for any outdoor plans.
 Bottom line: Winter is giving the Charlotte region an early hello!
